sections.h2: Where is Gillette, Wyoming, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Gillette is the county seat of Campbell County, in northeastern Wyoming, sitting in the Powder River Basin between the Bighorn Mountains to the west and the Black Hills to the east. The elevation is about 4,554 feet.

The city grew outward in stages. On January 1, 2018, Gillette annexed the Antelope Valley-Crestview area, which brought a large residential district inside city limits. Subdivisions such as Westover and Foothills, along with the Westover Road corridor, are part of the built-up area.

For a seller, the boundary matters more than it sounds. A house inside the city follows city zoning, city permits and city water and sewer rules. A house just outside it falls under Campbell County instead. The city planning staff say owners can petition to annex land that touches city limits, and service extensions are generally at the owner's expense.

sections.h2: How did Gillette start, and how fast has it grown?
sections.html:
Gillette began in 1891 as a railway town on the Chicago, Burlington and Quincy Railroad and was incorporated on January 6, 1892. It was named for Edward Gillette, a surveyor for the railroad company. Earlier names included Donkey Town and Rocky Pile.

A fire in November 1895 destroyed most of the young town. Growth came much later, tied to energy development. The population was 3,580 in 1960, 7,194 in 1970, 19,646 in 2000 and 33,403 in the 2020 census.

Most of that growth is recent, so Gillette has few very old houses. Sellers with homes from the growth decades should check the age of the roof, furnace and water heater before listing.

Coal, oil and coalbed methane gas have driven Gillette's economy for decades. Wyoming supplies close to 35 percent of the coal mined in the country, and much of it comes out of the Powder River Basin around Gillette.

A 2021 WyoFile report described how tied the county is to coal. Coal made up about 51.6 percent of Campbell County's assessed value in 2021, down from 58.6 percent in 2017, and assessed valuation fell by $850 million from 2020 to 2021. The same report said the two Arch Resources mines then employed 1,070 miners, and that Gillette College and the county were working on carbon technology, an industrial park and youth sports events to broaden the base.

Those numbers are from 2021, so check current figures. When mine employment or coal prices shift, local demand for houses can shift with it, and a seller who must move quickly may face a thinner pool of buyers.

  • Gillette is a regional center for media, education, health and arts, per its Wikipedia profile.
  • Wyoming's coal output matters nationally, so state and federal energy policy can reach Gillette household incomes.
  • Campbell County Memorial Hospital has 90 acute-care beds and is a certified area trauma hospital.

sections.h2: What does Gillette weather do to a house?
sections.html:
Gillette has cold winters, hot dry summers and enough hail to matter for roofs. The mean daily maximum in January is about 36 degrees Fahrenheit and the mean daily minimum is about 16. In July the mean maximum is about 86. The record high is 110 degrees and the record low is minus 40.

Annual precipitation averages about 17.6 inches, and annual snowfall averages about 55.7 inches. May is the wettest month, which lines up with the spring storm season.

On May 26, 2010, a hail storm moved through Gillette and hit the Westover and Foothills subdivisions hardest. The Gillette News-Record estimated the damage could top $46 million, including $28 million for roofs and gutters. Buyers in Gillette tend to look closely at roof age and gutters.

Freeze and thaw cycles also matter. Old windows, thin attic insulation and poor grading are worth checking before a buyer does.

sections.h2: Which schools, airport and transit serve Gillette?
sections.html:
Public schools in Gillette belong to Campbell County School District Number 1, which runs Campbell County High School and Thunder Basin High School. Gillette College, a two-year college, is also in town.

Northeast Wyoming Regional Airport has United flights operated by SkyWest, with about six daily flights to Denver. Jefferson Lines provides intercity bus service.

sections.h2: What permits and zoning rules affect a Gillette house sale?
sections.html:
Most structural work in Gillette needs a building permit and a zoning permit, and unpermitted work can complicate a sale. City planning staff say a garage or addition needs both after review by Building Inspection and Planning. Decks, sheds and retaining walls usually need both as well. A shed under 200 square feet or a retaining wall under 4 feet tall needs only the zoning permit.

Other city rules that show up in sales:

  • Fences need a free zoning permit. Front-yard fences are limited to 4 feet and side and rear fences to 6 feet.
  • Single-family zones allow only one residence per lot, so a second dwelling on the property is not permitted.
  • Homes need at least two paved off-street parking spaces.
  • Home businesses in residential zones need a Home Occupation Permit from Code Compliance.

You can look up zoning by calling the Planning Division at (307) 686-5281. Building Division contact is (307) 686-5200 or gillette@gillettewy.gov, and permits and inspections go through the city's online portal. If you inherit or buy a house that has a converted garage, an unpermitted deck or a rental unit in the basement, find out early whether the work can be legalized or whether a buyer will need to discount for it.

sections.h2: When are Campbell County property taxes due, and what exemptions exist?
sections.html:
Campbell County follows the state calendar. The first installment of the current year's tax is due September 1 and becomes delinquent after November 10 unless all taxes are paid by December 31. The second installment is due March 1 and becomes delinquent after May 10. The county treasurer mails tax bills on or before October 10.

Under Wyoming statute, unpaid balances accrue 18 percent annual interest. The statute text we read is a 2012 copy, so confirm current terms with the county.

Campbell County says homeowners, seniors and veterans can apply for 2027 exemptions from October 1, 2026 through March 1, 2027. The state Homeowner's Exemption removes 25 percent of taxable value on the first $1 million of fair market value for an owner-occupied primary residence, and the Long-term Homeowner's Exemption removes 50 percent on the first $3 million for owners 65 or older who have paid Wyoming residential property tax for at least 25 years. The veteran's exemption is a $6,000 reduction in assessed value, with a filing deadline of the fourth Monday in May.

If you sell during the year, ask your title company how current-year tax will be handled at closing. Offices to call: Treasurer (307) 682-7268 and Assessor (307) 682-7266.

sections.h2: How does a sale get recorded in Campbell County?
sections.html:
The Campbell County Clerk records deeds and keeps the grantor and grantee indexes. Under Wyoming Statute 18-3-402, the clerk stamps each instrument with the day, hour and minute it arrives, and the date of record is the filing date. The clerk will not record a document until the fee is paid. The Clerk's office phone is (307) 682-7285.

The Gillette planning FAQ also advises buyers to read the title report for easements, pre-annexation agreements and deed restrictions. A seller can save time by pulling the plat and any recorded agreements before listing.

If the house came through an estate, the paperwork that gives someone authority to sign the deed has to be in order before closing, so start that early.

sections.h2: What do Gillette sellers usually face, and how does a cash sale fit?
sections.html:
Gillette sellers commonly face aging roofs, deferred repairs, estate transfers and job moves. A cash sale works well when the owner wants to skip showings, repairs and a long financing contingency.

A cash offer from a company like ours is based on the house as it stands. We look at condition, location and the work a buyer would take on, and then we make an offer for you to accept or decline. There is no obligation, and we do not promise a specific price before we see the property.

  • Open-market listing: more exposure and often a higher price, with agent commission, repairs, showings and a financing timeline.
  • Cash sale: faster and simpler, usually at a lower price than a fully prepared listing.

Whichever route you choose, compare the numbers. If you owe back taxes, have a lien or are behind on a mortgage, tell us early, because those items change the closing steps.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Gillette house if it needs a new roof?
faqs.a: Yes. Hail has damaged many Gillette roofs, including the May 26, 2010 storm that hit Westover and Foothills. A cash buyer prices the roof into the offer, so you do not have to replace it before selling.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Campbell County?
faqs.a: The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1. Taxes become delinquent after November 10 and May 10, and paying everything by December 31 avoids interest on the first half. Call the Campbell County Treasurer at (307) 682-7268 to confirm your balance.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to sell a house with an unpermitted deck or garage in Gillette?
faqs.a: A permit is not required to sell, but unpermitted work can slow a sale or lower offers. The city says decks, additions and garages usually need building and zoning permits. Call the Building Division at (307) 686-5200 to ask whether work can be permitted after the fact.

faqs.q: Where are deeds recorded for a Gillette home?
faqs.a: Deeds are recorded with the Campbell County Clerk. The clerk stamps the date and time each instrument arrives and requires the fee in advance. The Clerk's office number is (307) 682-7285.

faqs.q: Does the Wyoming homeowner exemption affect my sale?
faqs.a: It lowers the taxable value while you live in the house as your primary residence, but it does not stop the sale. The 2027 filing window in Campbell County runs from October 1, 2026 to March 1, 2027. Ask your title company how tax is handled at closing.
